title: Apleno sequence file (.pseq)
description: A sequence is the flowchart of an Apleno app: a graph of steps executed one after another, starting from the single 'start' step and following each step's 'target'. The file is JSON, edited visually by the Apleno Sequence Editor.

cameraX.description: Editor view position (horizontal). Only used by the visual editor.

cameraY.description: Editor view position (vertical). Only used by the visual editor.

cameraZoom.description: Editor zoom level. Only used by the visual editor.

steps.description: All steps of the sequence. Exactly one step must have type 'start'. Step uuids must be unique.

uuid.description: Numeric identifier of the step, unique in the file. Other steps point to this step with 'target' / 'falsetarget'. Start at 1 and use the highest existing uuid + 1 for a new step.

id.description: Identifier usable from R/Python code to refer to this step, e.g. rpgm.step('main', 'form'). Not used for start/end steps. Must be unique in the sequence when not empty.

name.description: Name of the step displayed to the end user in the steps list. Not used for start/end steps.

type.description: 'start': entry point of the sequence (exactly one). 'rscript' (or its alias 'script'): runs an R (.R) or Python (.py) script file, the language depends on the file extension. 'gui': displays an interface (.pgui file) and waits for the user to submit it. 'condition': evaluates the R/Python expression 'r' and goes to 'target' if true, 'falsetarget' if false. 'sequence': jumps to another sequence (.pseq file) for good: it has no 'target', the app continues in that sequence and never comes back. 'end': ends the app.

x.description: Horizontal position of the step center in the visual editor. Steps are 200x50 and snap to a 50-unit grid; lay them out top to bottom about 150 units apart, with condition branches offset horizontally (e.g. 300 units).

y.description: Vertical position of the step center in the visual editor (y grows downward).

file.description: For 'rscript', 'gui' and 'sequence' steps: path of the file to run/display, relative to the project root folder (e.g. 'scripts/load.R', 'form.pgui', 'report.pseq').

r.description: For 'condition' steps: expression returning TRUE/True or FALSE/False, in the language given by 'language' (the key is named 'r' even for Python).

target.description: uuid of the next step (for a condition: the step to go to when the expression is true). Required for every step type except 'end' and 'sequence', which have no exit.

falsetarget.description: For 'condition' steps: uuid of the step to go to when the expression is false.
